The interface locale, the law language, and the search jurisdiction are separate values. A browser language can suggest en, nl, ar, or ja for the interface. It does not select a place or a jurisdiction. A language tag or a two- or three-letter code is rejected as a jurisdiction id. An explicit internal id such as netherlands or place:netherlands is kept.

Civil dates keep year, month, or day precision. A missing part is not filled in. A finer requested precision than the value contains is unknown. English, Dutch, and Arabic month names come from the locale catalogs. Japanese dates use numeric months. A civil date is not shifted by a timezone. An instant becomes a civil day only in a timezone the caller names. IANA zones use Intl.DateTimeFormat formatToParts. The browser timezone is not read.

Original titles keep the direction of the law text. Arabic and Hebrew titles are rtl. Japanese, Chinese, and Korean titles are CJK and ltr, including inside an Arabic interface. Latin identifiers inside an rtl title are isolated. Machine and official translations use the catalogue label. Any other kind stays the generic translation label. The original title remains. A translation is not a source revision.

The Japanese catalogue key included_because is 収録した理由, matching the interaction contract. A supplied reason is joined with a fullwidth colon. English, Dutch, and Arabic join the same label and reason with a space. The reason text is not rewritten.
